paper.title: A data-driven approach for learning to control computers
paper.central_claim: Scaling human demonstrations with a shared keyboard/mouse interface and straightforward BC+RL yields state-of-the-art, human-level mean performance across MiniWoB++ and strong cross-task transfer, suggesting a route toward general computer control.

provenance.session_id_reason: No independently exposed worker session ID.

sections_read: Entire fixed extracted text including all supplied methods, results, references and appendices
materials.version_binding: Manifest binds version; extraction SOURCE header is unversioned. Figures available through supplied captions/prose, not a separate image audit.

evidence.quote: This is a combination that was proposed at MiniWob’s conception
evidence.support_explanation: Prior BC+RL shortfall and specialized-action/curriculum lineage; this is the paper’s account, not an independent audit of ancestors.

evidence.quote: the primary missing factor in achieving high performance is simply the size of the human trajectory dataset used for behavioural cloning
evidence.support_explanation: Empirical pivot: data quantity, rather than necessary special-purpose algorithms, is proposed as the missing ingredient.

evidence.quote: We choose instead to use only mouse and keyboard based actions.
evidence.support_explanation: Keyboard/mouse action compatibility is an actual interface choice; broad transfer remains a hypothesis.

evidence.quote: we give our agent access to an environment-provided dictionary of text strings
evidence.support_explanation: Environment-provided task-field dictionary is privileged information.

evidence.quote: An 8-layer multimodal transformer combines pixel and language embeddings, whose output is concatenated with an embedding of the previous action and passed through 2 LSTMs.
evidence.support_explanation: Actual multimodal transformer, LSTM, and four policy outputs.

evidence.quote: We have not run LSTM ablations in the final configuration
evidence.support_explanation: Final memory contribution is not causally isolated.

evidence.quote: We collected over 2.4 million demonstrations of the 104 104 MiniWob ++ tasks from a total of 77 77 human participants, which amounts to approximately 6300 6300 hours.
evidence.support_explanation: Human data scale and participant denominator.

evidence.quote: In our work we consider the former with equal weighting to the BC and RL losses
evidence.support_explanation: Equal-weight simultaneous BC and VMPO training.

evidence.quote: our human demonstration data was split into train and test sets (2.2 million & 310 thousand episodes respectively)
evidence.support_explanation: Episode split; not heldout task split.

evidence.quote: tasks where the final reward was less than 0.5 0.5 were removed
evidence.support_explanation: Selection by environment terminal reward, not a learned judge.

evidence.quote: We were furthermore only able to run one seed for each of the conditions that we report in this paper.
evidence.support_explanation: Only one seed per setting.

evidence.quote: our agent achieves human-level mean performance across the suite of MiniWob ++ tasks
evidence.support_explanation: Author-reported mean human parity, not per-task or broader-platform parity.

evidence.quote: our agent fails to get any score for two tasks: simon-says , and terminal
evidence.support_explanation: Explicit zero-performing task boundary.

evidence.quote: with a fixed budget of training steps per task, training one agent on all 104 MiniWob ++ tasks leads to a strong boost in performance compared to training separate agents on each task
evidence.support_explanation: Transfer experiment co-trains all104 tasks; no unseen-task evaluation.

evidence.quote: we simply reduced the relative weight of the BC loss (scaled by the square root of the relative size) to slow overfitting
evidence.support_explanation: Dataset size intervention is accompanied by BC loss reweighting.

evidence.quote: a 75% drop in performance if this input is removed
evidence.support_explanation: Dominant DOM dependence limits generic pixel-only control inference.

evidence.quote: there is a significant mismatch between our recorded human trajectories and the actions available to the agent
evidence.support_explanation: DOM-action control has human-trajectory/action mismatch.

evidence.quote: Reward information is thus low-noise, undelayed, and available in large quantities.
evidence.support_explanation: Low-noise benchmark reward and scripted goal semantics.

evidence.quote: Maximum number of steps per episode | 300
evidence.support_explanation: Episode max-step protocol.

evidence.quote: Some scores from these studies were only available in figure format and were therefore estimated as accurately as possible.
evidence.support_explanation: External scores include digitized figures; cross-paper harness fairness limited.

evidence.quote: we filter the 16 out of 104 tasks without external scores
evidence.support_explanation: Matched external subset and composite best-per-task external baseline disclosed.

evidence.quote: most likely due to network-related control latency
evidence.support_explanation: Human comparator affected by latency.

evidence.quote: We instead interface directly with the Chrome DevTools Protocol (CDP)
evidence.support_explanation: Changed environment interface.

signatures.information: Task text, privileged DOM and task-field dictionary,165×220 pixels, previous action and recurrent state.
signatures.operation: Tokenize text and encode pixels; transformer fusion; two-layer LSTM; emit mouse/keyboard action type plus conditional arguments.
signatures.output: 10 action types; discretized51×51 cursor coordinates; keyboard index or task-field index.
signatures.conditions: Human and policy use compatible keyboard/mouse interface; text/DOM remain available.
signatures.feedback: Programmatic task reward and next observation.
signatures.selection_rule: No online self-modification selection; static policy architecture.
signatures.data: All104 synthetic task families; demonstrations and online rollouts.
signatures.persistence: Learned parameters persist after training; within-episode LSTM state is not cross-task experience memory.
signatures.later_use: Same policy evaluated on randomized instances of trained task families.
signatures.claimed_effect: General control interface allows scalable imitation plus RL.
signatures.failure_boundary: DOM ablation loses75%;2Hz misses simon-says events; terminal fails; actual non-browser transfer not tested.

signatures.object: Demonstration prior and online reward training
signatures.information: Human actions, task terminal rewards, train/validation episode split.
signatures.operation: Filter demonstration reward below0.5 and up to10 consecutive no-ops; jointly optimize BC and VMPO with equal losses; uniformly sample demonstrations across all tasks.
signatures.conditions: Millions of human episodes, plentiful low-noise synthetic rewards, compatible action semantics.
signatures.feedback: BC labels plus environment RL reward; heldout demonstration likelihood diagnoses overfit.
signatures.selection_rule: Demonstration acceptance reward≥0.5; no-op removal; hyperparameters hand-tuned with limited runs.
signatures.data: 2.4m collected;2.2m train/310k test before success filtering,77 people,~6300h.
signatures.persistence: Parameter learning; no library of selected code edits or retained plans.
signatures.claimed_effect: Larger demonstration support rescues straightforward BC+RL; co-training improves per-task sample efficiency.
signatures.failure_boundary: Scaling changes BC weight;1seed; same task families appear in training and testing.

claims.text: Human-level mean MiniWoB performance and state-of-the-art across task suite.
claims.setting: CC-Net multimodal recurrent policy;104 synthetic task families; DOM/task-field privileges; online execution.
claims.baseline: Humans and composite best published taskwise scores; BC-only and RL-only variants.
claims.control: Within-architecture loss ablations; external interfaces/datasets/harnesses differ.
claims.selection_vs_test: 2.2m/310k demonstration episode split, not family holdout; hand tuning and one training seed.
claims.result: Reported mean matches human mean, exceeds composite external mean; not all tasks human-level.
claims.denominator: 104 own tasks;88 external-comparable tasks after16 exclusions; full taskwise table.
claims.allowed_conclusion: Strong author-reported closed-loop performance on trained MiniWoB families, not human-equivalent general computer control.

claims.text: Data size is the primary missing factor and co-training yields strong cross-task transfer.
claims.setting: Vary demonstration size; compare all-task versus individual-task learning at equal per-task frames.
claims.baseline: Small-data BC+RL, BC-only, RL-only and individual-task agents.
claims.control: Current architecture fixed for scaling; BC weight changes with sqrt(data ratio), so not pure data intervention.
claims.selection_vs_test: All104 task families jointly trained; new randomized instances do not constitute unused-environment transfer.
claims.result: More data improves results through full dataset; multi-task improves efficiency on trained tasks.
claims.denominator: 104-task averages, one training seed/configuration;2bn-frame scaling snapshot.
claims.allowed_conclusion: Data support and cross-task sharing matter in this setting; no unique data-only causal effect or unseen-task transfer established.
